chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from whom he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'Or what your right hands possess [the keys] of.' He said: 'A man may have an agent who manages his wealth and eats from it without his permission.'
ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic phrase 'what your right hands possess the keys of' mean in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to elucidate the legal scope of 'what your right hands possess the keys of' within the context of permissible consumption. The Imam clarifies that this phrase extends to an agent (*wakil*) who manages a principal's wealth and consumes it without explicit permission, thereby establishing a specific juristic category for unauthorized but permissible use of entrusted assets. This interpretation highlights the flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding agency (*wilayah*) and the distinction between ownership and possession in commercial transactions.
